title: Adding and subtracting
description:
Write these functions (arguments in `rdi`, `rsi`, `rdx`; result in `rax`):

| Function | Result |
|---|---|
| `add_sub(a, b, c)` | a + b − c |
| `negate(x)` | −x |
| `plus_two(x)` | x + 2, with two `inc` |
| `distance(a, b)` | b − a (it may be negative) |
| `add32(a, b)` | a + b done in **32-bit** registers, so it wraps at 2³²: `add32(0xFFFFFFFF, 1)` is 0 |

starter.solution.asm:
add_sub:
        mov     rax, rdi
        ret

negate:
        mov     rax, rdi
        ret

plus_two:
        mov     rax, rdi
        ret

distance:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

add32:
        mov     rax, rdi
        add     rax, rsi
        ret

solution.solution.asm:
add_sub:
        mov     rax, rdi
        add     rax, rsi
        sub     rax, rdx
        ret

negate:
        mov     rax, rdi
        neg     rax
        ret

plus_two:
        mov     rax, rdi
        inc     rax
        inc     rax
        ret

distance:
        mov     rax, rsi
        sub     rax, rdi
        ret

add32:
        mov     eax, edi
        add     eax, esi
        ret

hints: Start each function with `mov rax, rdi`, then add or subtract the others. `neg rax` makes −x.
For `add32`, do the addition in `eax` (`mov eax, edi` then `add eax, esi`): a 32-bit result wraps at 2³² and clears the upper half of `rax`.
unitTests:
test "add_sub"
    add_sub(10, 5, 3) == 12
    add_sub(0, 0, 1) == -1
    add_sub(-10, -10, -30) == 10
test "negate"
    negate(5) == -5
    negate(-123456789012) == 123456789012
    negate(0) == 0
test "plus_two"
    plus_two(40) == 42
    plus_two(-2) == 0
test "distance"
    distance(3, 10) == 7
    distance(10, 3) == -7
test "add32 wraps at 32 bits"
    add32(1, 2) == 3
    add32(0xFFFFFFFF, 1) == 0
    add32(0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF) == 0xFFFFFFFE
    add32(0x100000005, 1) == 6
lessonTitle: add, sub, inc, dec and neg
